headline: Developer Runs a 28.9M-Parameter Language Model on an $8 Microcontroller
what_happened: Developer slvDev built and open-sourced a 28.9-million-parameter language model that runs entirely on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller costing roughly $8, generating short stories at about 9.5 tokens per second with no network connection. Using 4-bit quantization and a Gemma-derived technique that keeps most weights in flash memory instead of scarce RAM, the 14.9MB model ships with full firmware, training code, and on-chip benchmark results under an MIT license.
why_it_matters: It's a concrete demonstration that useful language models can run entirely offline on sub-$10 hardware, no cloud or GPU required -- a data point for the broader trend of pushing AI inference onto tiny, cheap edge devices rather than relying on datacenter-scale compute.
one_liner: A developer got a tiny AI model to write simple stories entirely on an $8 computer chip, with no internet connection needed.
